summary.text: 个 is used today mainly as a general classifier for individual people and things. Traditional accounts associate it with bamboo-related 箇 and report 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo, but do not establish a complete graphic path to the modern character.

formation.text: Treat modern 个 as a whole graph. In the transmitted analysis of related 箇, 竹 marks the bamboo category and 固 supplies a sound cue. A commentary reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo; this does not show that the modern classifier was borrowed from the spoken name of a bamboo object.

components.text: Treat 个 here as a whole graph, not as a tally 丨 combined with a person 人. That proposed breakdown is not established as its historical construction.
In the related graph 箇, 竹 marks the bamboo category in the transmitted analysis. The curated image shows 箇 with 竹 above 固; it illustrates that analysis, not a dated stage in 个’s graphic history.

In 箇, the transmitted analysis identifies 固 as the sound element. Reported Old Chinese forms 固 *[k]ˤa-s and 箇 *kˤa[r]-s have a similar, but not identical, pattern. This comparison alone does not establish the component’s role or the spoken name of a bamboo object.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison reports 固 *[k]ˤa-s through a secondary source and 箇 *kˤa[r]-s in Baxter–Sagart, but no directly verified same-system reading for 固. It shows reported similarity, not independent proof of the transmitted analysis or a bamboo object’s name.

sound.text: These reported Old Chinese forms are similar but not identical; the cited material does not independently verify a same-system reading for 固.

history.text: The curated image is a modern redraw of 箇 in a transmitted Shuowen seal-script style, with 竹 above 固. It illustrates the traditional analysis, not a securely dated stage in the graphic history of 个.

A transmitted lexicographic account reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo, while a variant dictionary catalogs 个 as a variant of 個. These accounts do not document a complete graphic sequence linking 箇, 個, and modern 个.

uncertainties.text: The available records do not establish a character-specific oracle-bone or bronze form, or a dated graphic path from the bamboo-related account to modern 个. This does not show that earlier forms never existed.

Bamboo-related and ritual counting uses are recorded, but their chronology and a continuous development into the general classifier are not established. A research abstract proposes a more complex history.
No independently recoverable spoken name for the proposed bamboo object is established. Similar reported readings make sound-based borrowing possible, but do not demonstrate it.

senses.text: A transmitted commentary reports this meaning for 个 as an alternate form; it is not independently established as the character’s earliest meaning.
A cited classical passage is associated by commentary with counting bamboo. It does not establish the first attestation or a transition to the general classifier.

senses.gloss: counting item or unit, like 枚
senses.text: A ritual counting context is recorded, with 个 glossed as comparable to 枚. The available evidence does not date this sense or connect it to bamboo-related counting.

senses.gloss: general classifier for individual people or things
senses.text: 个 is used as a general classifier for counting people and objects. Its emergence is not dated here.
A current sense meaning “single” or “individual” is recorded. Its historical relation to the classifier is not established here.

limitations.text: The recorded historical counting uses cannot be placed in a secure sequence, and no semantic bridge from bamboo-related counting to general classifier use is established; no development is asserted.
Modern dictionaries also record demonstrative and particle uses, but no dated sequence connects them to the older counting uses.
